artists.biography:
Yello is a Swiss electronica band consisting of Dieter Meier and Boris Blank. They are probably best known for their singles "The Race" and "Oh Yeah", which feature a mix of electronic music and manipulated vocals, as does most of their music.

The band was originally formed by Boris Blank (keyboards, sampling, percussion, backing vocals) and Carlos PerÃ³n (tapes) in the late 1970s. Dieter Meier (vocals, lyrics), a millionaire industrialist and gambler, was brought in when the two founders realized that they needed a singer. The new band name, Yello, was chosen as a pun based on a statement made by Dieter Meier, "a yelled Hello". Yello's first release was the 1979 single "I.T. Splash". The LP Solid Pleasure, featuring the hit dance single "Bostich", was released in November 1980.

In 1983, Yello received substantial media attention with the release of "I Love You" and "Lost Again". PerÃ³n left the band in 1983 to start a solo career. With their 1983 album You Gotta Say Yes to Another Excess, the band began a working relationship with Ernst Gamper, whose "corner cut" logo would represent them for three albums, and who would design covers for the group beyond the demise of this logo.

Meier is also a filmmaker, having written and directed the films Jetzt und Alles and Lightmaker as well as most of Yello's music videos. Additionally, Meier produces his own wine on his ranch.

In 2005, Yello re-released their early albums Solid Pleasure, Claro Que Si, You Gotta Say Yes to Another Excess, Stella, One Second, and Flag, all with rare bonus tracks, as part of the Yello Remaster Series.

A documentary on Yello, Electro Pop made in Switzerland, directed by Anka Schmid, was premiered at the Riff Raff cinema in ZÃ¼rich in September 2005.
Yello was commissioned to produce music for the launch of the Audi A5 at the Geneva Motor Show in March 2007 and for the Audi A5 commercial in May 2007.

Released in 2021, Yell40 Years is a retrospective compilation by the Swiss electronic duo Yello, celebrating four decades of their innovative career. The album spans their signature blend of electronic and pop music, showcasing their pioneering use of synthesizers, quirky rhythms, and playful sound design. The tracklist features iconic hits such as "Oh Yeah," "Vicious Games," "Desire," and "The Rhythm Divine" (featuring Shirley Bassey), alongside fan favorites and select collaborations, reflecting the band's evolution from their early experimental roots to their later, more polished productions.

As a career-spanning collection, Yell40 Years is structured to highlight both the energetic, dance-oriented side of Yello and their more melodic, cinematic moments. The deluxe edition, released as a 4CD set, includes a "Mellow Yello" disc focusing on atmospheric and lesser-known tracks, offering a comprehensive overview of their artistic range. Issued by Polydor and Universal Music Group, the compilation was well-received for its thoughtful curation and high-quality remastering, serving as both an introduction for new listeners and a definitive anthology for longtime fans.
